intellectual_tradition: Yangming School of Mind (synthesizer of Lu-Wang tradition), from Yuyao, Zhejiang; founder of Yaojiang School, ancestor of Taizhou School and Japanese Yangming studies
historical_significance: 王阳明（1472—1529），名守仁，字伯安，浙江余姚人，明代最杰出的思想家、教育家、军事家，心学集大成者。弘治十二年进士，因得罪刘瑾谪贬贵州龙场驿丞，于龙场悟道，确立'心即理'宗旨。后任南赣巡抚平定匪乱，仅三十五日平定宁王朱宸濠之乱，创立'致良知'学说。晚年提出'知行合一''四句教'（无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动，知善知恶是良知，为善去恶是格物），天泉证道确立晚年定论。其学上承陆九渊'心即理'，下启泰州学派与日本阳明学，打破朱子学'析心与理为二'的格局，强调'心外无物、心外无理'，圣人之道吾性自足。用兵'此心不动，随机而动'，以良知用兵，声东击西、攻心为上。代表作《传习录》《大学问》《王文成公全书》。
famous_quote: Unity of knowledge and action: knowing is the beginning of action, action is the completion of knowing; Extending innate knowledge: that bit of innate knowing is your own criterion; Unmoved mind acting on circumstances; Four-sentence teaching: Mind substance is neither good nor evil, intention stirring has good and evil, innate knowing knows good and evil, rectifying affairs is doing good and removing evil
influence: Wang Yangming (1472-1529), courtesy name Shouren, from Yuyao, Zhejiang, was the Ming dynasty's most distinguished philosopher, educator, and military strategist, and the crowning synthesizer of the School of Mind. A jinshi of 1499, he was exiled to Longchang, Guizhou after offending eunuch Liu Jin; there he attained enlightenment, establishing that 'mind is principle.' As Grand Coordinator of southern Jiangxi he suppressed banditry, and in just thirty-five days quelled Prince Ning's rebellion, developing his doctrine of 'extending innate knowledge.' His final teaching crystallized in the Four-Sentence Teaching and the Tianquan verification. Breaking Zhu Xi's separation of mind and principle, he taught that there is nothing outside the mind; the way of the sage is self-sufficient in one's own nature. In war he practiced 'an unmoved mind, acting according to circumstances.' Major works: Chuanxilu, Da Xue Wen, and the Complete Works.

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》徐爱录：心即理也。天下又有心外之事、心外之理乎？《年谱》：始知圣人之道，吾性自足，向之求理于事物者误也。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu (Instructions for Practical Living), record of Xu Ai: "Mind is principle. Is there any affair or principle outside the mind?" Nianpu (Chronological Biography): "Only now do I know that the way of the sage is complete within my own nature; to seek principle in external things was an error."
mode_evidence.source: 始知圣人之道，吾性自足，向之求理于事物者误也。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》下：你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂；你来看此花时，则此花颜色一时明白起来。便知此花不在你的心外。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 3: "Before you look at these flowers, they and your mind both return to silence; when you look at them, their colors become clear all at once. Thus you know these flowers are not outside your mind."
mode_evidence.source: 你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂；你来看此花时，则此花颜色一时明白起来。便知此花不在你的心外。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》徐爱录：未有知而不行者，知而不行，只是未知。……知是行的主意，行是知的功夫；知是行之始，行是知之成。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, record of Xu Ai: "There has never been one who knows yet does not act; knowing without acting is simply not yet knowing... Knowledge is the master of action; action is the work of knowledge. Knowledge is the beginning of action; action is the completion of knowledge."
mode_evidence.source: 未有知而不行者，知而不行，只是未知。……知是行的主意，行是知的功夫；知是行之始，行是知之成。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》下：尔那一点良知，是尔自家底准则。尔意念着处，他是便知是，非便知非，更瞒他一些不得。《与杨仕德薛尚谦书》：破山中贼易，破心中贼难。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 3: "That bit of innate knowing of yours is your own criterion. Where your thought alights, it knows right as right and wrong as wrong, and none can deceive it." Letter to Yang Shide and Xue Shangqian: "It is easy to defeat bandits in the mountains, hard to defeat the bandit in one's own heart."
mode_evidence.source: 破山中贼易，破心中贼难。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》下（天泉证道）：无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动，知善知恶是良知，为善去恶是格物。……二君之见正好相资为用，不可各执一边。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 3 (Tianquan verification before the disciples): "The substance of the mind is neither good nor evil; the stirring of intention has good and evil; knowing good and evil is innate knowing; doing good and removing evil is the investigation of things... Your two views are exactly complementary; neither side should be clung to alone."
mode_evidence.source: 无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动，知善知恶是良知，为善去恶是格物。……二君之见正好相资为用，不可各执一边。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》下：人须在事上磨，方立得住；方能静亦定，动亦定。《传习录》上：省察是有事时存养，存养是无事时省察。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 3: "One must grind in the midst of affairs to stand firm—only then is one settled both in stillness and in motion." Chuanxilu, Part 1: "Self-examination is preservation-cultivation when affairs are present; preservation-cultivation is self-examination when affairs are absent."
mode_evidence.source: 省察是有事时存养，存养是无事时省察。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》上：吾辈用功，只求日减，不求日增。减得一分人欲，便是复得一分天理，何等轻快脱洒，何等简易！《传习录》上：圣人之心如明镜，只是一个明，则随感而应，无物不照。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 1: "In our effort we should only seek daily reduction, not daily increase. To reduce one part of human desire is to recover one part of heavenly principle—how light, how free and easy, how simple!" Chuanxilu, Part 1: "The mind of the sage is like a clear mirror: only its clarity matters, and it responds to whatever comes, reflecting all things."
mode_evidence.source: 圣人之心如明镜，只是一个明，则随感而应，无物不照。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》下：人要随才成就，才是其所能为。……如良医之治病，随其疾之虚实强弱寒热内外而斟酌加减。《训蒙大意示教读刘伯颂等》：诱之歌诗以发其志意，导之习礼以肃其威仪，讽之读书以开其知觉。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 3: "People should be brought to accomplishment according to their talent, so that what they can do is realized... like a good physician treating illness, weighing and adjusting according to whether the condition is deficient or replete, strong or weak, cold or hot, internal or external." Xunmeng Dayi (On Instructing the Young): "Lure them with songs and poems to stir their resolve; guide them in practicing ritual to order their bearing; have them recite texts to open their awareness."
mode_evidence.source: 诱之歌诗以发其志意，导之习礼以肃其威仪，讽之读书以开其知觉。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《传习录》下：用兵何术？但学问纯笃，养得此心不动，乃术尔。凡人智能相去不甚远，胜负之决，不待卜诸临阵，只在此心动与不动之间。《年谱》：先设间以离其党……而亲率兵趋南昌。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Chuanxilu, Part 3: "What is the art of warfare? Only that when learning is pure and sincere and this mind is unmoved, that is the art. The intelligence of ordinary people does not differ greatly; victory or defeat is not decided by divination on the battlefield, but only in whether this mind is moved or unmoved." Nianpu: "First he sent spies to split the enemy's partisans... then personally led troops toward Nanchang."
mode_evidence.source: 先设间以离其党……而亲率兵趋南昌。

mode_evidence.evidence_zh: 《大学问》：大人者，以天地万物为一体者也。……是故见孺子之入井，而必有怵惕恻隐之心焉，是其仁之与孺子而为一体也。《传习录》中《答顾东桥书》拔本塞源之论。
mode_evidence.evidence_en: Daxuewen (Inquiry on the Great Learning): "The great man regards Heaven, Earth, and the ten thousand things as one body... Therefore, seeing a child about to fall into a well, he necessarily has a heart of alarm and compassion—this is his benevolence forming one body with the child." Chuanxilu, Part 2, Reply to Gu Dongqiao: the discourse on pulling up the roots and stopping up the source.
mode_evidence.source: 大人者，以天地万物为一体者也。……是故见孺子之入井，而必有怵惕恻隐之心焉，是其仁之与孺子而为一体也。《传习录》中《答顾东桥书》拔本塞源之论。

cross_references.description_zh: 心即理 vs 性即理：王阳明批评朱子'析心与理为二'，主张理不在事物而在吾心；朱子格物穷理是外向认识论，阳明格物正念头是内向实践论。这是宋明理学'理学'与'心学'两系的分水岭。
cross_references.description_en: Mind-is-Principle vs Nature-is-Principle: Wang criticized Zhu Xi's splitting of mind and principle; Zhu's investigation of things is outward-directed epistemology, Wang's is inward-directed praxis. This is the watershed between Neo-Confucian rationalism and the School of Mind.

cross_references.description_zh: 王阳明承陆九渊'心即理''六经注我'之旨，以'致良知'完成心学体系化；陆发其端而未畅，阳明扩充到底，故并称'陆王心学'。
cross_references.description_en: Wang inherited Lu Jiuyuan's 'mind is principle' and 'the classics annotate me,' completing the systematization of the School of Mind through 'extending innate knowledge'; hence the joint name Lu-Wang.

cross_references.description_zh: 王阳明自述'所学皆由孔子之统绪'，知行合一与万物一体之仁直承孔子'吾道一以贯之'与仁学传统。
cross_references.description_en: Wang claimed his learning continued Confucius's line: unity of knowledge and action and the benevolence of all-things-one-body carry forward 'my way is strung on one thread' and the ren tradition.

cross_references.description_zh: 王阳明'满街都是圣人'的人人皆可为圣论，与黄宗羲以《明夷待访录》批判君主专制一脉相通：黄宗羲师承刘宗周，刘宗周承阳明蕺山一系，阳明学的心性平等观为明清批判思想提供了内在资源。
cross_references.description_en: Wang's doctrine that 'the whole street is full of sages' connects to Huang Zongxi's critique of despotism: Huang, heir of Liu Zongzhou in the Yangming line, drew on the Yangming view of moral equality of all minds.

cross_references.description_zh: 良知内在自律 vs 天人感应他律：董仲舒以超验之天制约君权，王阳明以人人内在良知作为道德最高法庭。外在权威与内在权威构成中国政治伦理思想史的两极。
cross_references.description_en: Innate-conscience autonomy vs heaven-human heteronomy: Dong constrained rulers through transcendent Heaven; Wang made each person's innate moral knowing the supreme court. External versus internal authority as two poles of Chinese ethical-political thought.

cross_references.description_zh: 王阳明'心外无物'与司马迁'究天人之际'：两者都把探究焦点从外在天命转向人的世界——司马迁转向历史人事，王阳明转向本心良知。
cross_references.description_en: Wang's 'nothing outside the mind' and Sima Qian's 'probing heaven and humanity': both shifted inquiry from external mandate to the human world—Sima to history and affairs, Wang to the mind's innate knowing.

modern_value_zh: 知行合一——执行力思维：把'知道但做不到'重新定义为'并不真知道'，倒逼承诺升级
致良知——内在道德法庭：在复杂情境中首先问'此刻良知知不知是非'，再谈利害计算
心即理——内在主权思维：把判断的最终根据收回自己心中，适用于信息过载时代'谁替我做决定'的问题
事上磨练——实战历练思维：把每一次冲突、挫败、被误解重新定义为'磨练科目'
减法存理——极简方法论：问'我该停止做什么'而非'我还能加什么'，把问题归结为去除障碍
modern_value_en: Unity of knowledge and action: redefine 'knowing but not doing' as 'not truly knowing,' forcing commitment upgrade
Extending innate knowledge: the inner moral court—ask first 'does liangzhi know right and wrong here?' before calculating interests
Mind as principle: reclaim the final ground of judgment to your own mind—an answer to decision outsourcing in the information age
Refinement through affairs: reframe every conflict, setback, and misunderstanding as 'tempering practice'
Subtractive preservation of principle: ask 'what should I stop doing?' not 'what else can I add,' reducing problems to obstacle removal
place_of_origin: Shaoxing Prefecture, Yuyao County (now Yuyao, Zhejiang)
unique_thing: Wang Yangming's core achievement was 'a total mobilization of thought': he moved the 'external heavenly principle' of Neo-Confucianism back into the human mind—'mind is principle,' 'nothing outside the mind,' 'my nature is self-sufficient'—thus relocating moral authority from external classics to inner illumination. He was not just a armchair philosopher but a military genius with real power—quelling Prince Ning's rebellion in thirty-five days with 'an unmoved mind, acting according to circumstances'; he used the 'Four-Sentence Teaching' as his final doctrine, a framework integrating both sudden and gradual paths. He proved: thought need not be suspended in abstraction, philosophy can govern—the greatest legacy of Yangming studies is the command of 'unity of knowledge and action': knowing and doing cannot be separated in concept, true knowing necessarily entails doing.
